landing.heroTitle: The week, on the fridge, in your own handwriting
landing.heroBody: Set a handful of parameters and print a skeleton: one week, seven days top to bottom, every day the same height. Then it is paper. No app to open, no account, nothing to sync, nothing that runs out of battery on a Tuesday.
landing.howTitle: Three minutes once, then a pen for the rest of the term
landing.step1Body: One to six people. Each picks a symbol — the cat, the rocket, the flower — or takes their initial. A house stands for the whole household. Pre-readers find themselves by the picture.
landing.step2Body: Leave the dates blank and print a term's worth in one go, or set a week and get the week number, the range and each day's date printed. Same layout either way. Black on whatever paper is in the tray.
landing.step3Title: Circle a mark, write the thing
landing.step3Body: Every writing line starts with the whole household's marks. Circle one and the line belongs to that person; circle the house and it belongs to everyone. Any line can be anyone's, so a busy Thursday does not overflow a fixed box.
meta.homeDescription: A free printable weekly planner for family life: seven equal days, filled in by hand and stuck on the fridge. No app, no account — just paper and a pen.
meta.builderDescription: Set up your family, give each child a symbol, and print a weekly sheet for the fridge. A4 or Letter, 15 languages, free and no account.
meta.aboutDescription: What Fridgeweek is, who it is for, and what happens to your data — which is close to nothing. A small open-source project for families, free under MIT.
meta.notFoundDescription: That page does not exist. Go back to Fridgeweek and make a printable weekly sheet for the fridge.
footer.pitch: Fridgeweek is open source and free forever. Read every line of it, report a bug, or add your own language —
footer.pitchLink: the whole project is on GitHub
footer.legal: MIT licence · no cookies · privacy-friendly analytics
landing.heroFacts: Free · MIT · A4 and Letter · {count} sheet languages
landing.setTitle: Nine choices, and the layout does the arithmetic
landing.setBody: Fridgeweek never shrinks a line behind your back. If a configuration will not fit on the paper, it says so and tells you exactly what to change.
landing.samplesTitle: Two real sheets, exactly as they print
landing.endsUpBody: Circle the mark, write the thing, cross it out when it is done. Print one on Sunday evening, or twenty at the start of term.
